question.text: If valuation deviation between two consecutive valuations at asset level exceeds WHAT percentage, IM must inform investors with reasons?

answer.text: 20% at each asset level (or 33% in a financial year)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 5.16.6 (Valuation) and Ch 8 requirements, deviation > 20% between consecutive valuations (or > 33% in a financial year) triggers investor disclosure. The Trap: 5%/10%/50% are not the prescribed thresholds. Cross-Exam Context: Consistent with the valuation circular referenced in Ch 5. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Document the reasoning for material deviations immediately; regulators focus heavily on this disclosure.
